title: Revise visual density token set for dataviz and compact controls
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: create a tightened visual-density token set targeted at data visualization components (charts, legends, small tables) and compact control surfaces (dense toolbars, list rows, compact buttons). This change will adjust color ramp stops for high-contrast chart palettes, compress the type scale's intermediate sizes, reduce spacing and corner radii for compact mode, and rebalance shadow/elevation so depth cues remain legible at smaller scales. Scope excludes global product tokens for large-screen layouts; this is an additive compact mode token pack that can be opt-in per component.
acceptance_criteria: Compact token set is defined in tokens/compact-mode/ with names matching token naming conventions
Charts show no more than 12% drop in color distinguishability (measured by contrast+palette delta) vs baseline and maintain accessibility for primary/secondary series
Dense table row height reduced by 14px on compact tokens without clipping content or causing horizontal scroll at standard column widths
Buttons in compact variant use new radius and spacing tokens and pass visual regression tests across tiers
Shadow/elevation values updated such that at compact scales focus outlines and elevation separation meet 3:1 contrast with background
design_notes: Introduced palette 'compact-accent' with four stops: primary, accent-muted, series-2, series-3; tuned primarily for small mark visibility
Reduced type scale step between body-1 and body-2 from 2.5px to 1.5px for tighter rhythm in dense lists
Defined spacing tokens: s-xxs (4px), s-xs (6px), s-sm (8px) to replace previous small gaps in compact components
Corner radii: compact-radius-xs = 4px, compact-radius-sm = 6px; applied only to compact variants to avoid token collision
Shadows: flattened ambient shadow stop and increased penumbra contrast at compact elevation levels to preserve perceived depth
Left charts' tick/label density option: use compact typography tokens + horizontal padding token to avoid overlap
This update is additive—existing default tokens remain unchanged; component variants will opt into compact tokens via a single feature flag
tradeoffs: Tighter type scale improves information density but increases risk of legibility issues across some low-DPI monitors; mitigated via accessibility audits and fallback spacing tokens
Compressed radii and spacing reduce perceived affordance for touch targets; we limit compact buttons to desktop/secondary actions and keep primary CTAs at default sizes
Palette compression risks color collisions for complex multi-series charts; we recommend series grouping and emphasize pattern legends when >4 series are present
